item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Fri Aug 7 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Fri Aug 7 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: Home Away from Home: Student Life on Campus — Fri Aug 7, 9:00 AM — HERMAN B WELLS LIBRARY
item.description:
Spanning across four decades—1970s to the 2000s—items including scrapbooks, photographs, student papers, and handbooks demonstrate life on and off campus. item.title: McCalla Open Gallery Hours — Fri Aug 7, 11:00 AM — McCalla Building
item.description: Outfitting IU Athletics: Hoosier Champions This exhibit showcases objects from IU's championship teams and athletes, connecting them to historic achievements in the Big Ten and the national stage. The items featured in the exhibit are from the IU Athletics Sports Memorabilia Collection and feature photos and videos provided by IU Athletics and Indiana University Archives. Dates: November 14, 2025 - October 2026 By Their Own Hands: The Black Filmmakers Hall of Fame! Founded in 1974 by the Culture and Ethnic Affairs Guild of the Oakland Museum of California, the Black Filmmakers Hall of Fame began as a film lecture series and awards ceremony celebrating achievements of Black film industry figures. When that organization closed, they donated their materials to IU. In collaboration with the IU Black Film Center and Archive, this exhibit features objects from that collection, including founding documents, costumes

item.title: Terran Robotics 3D Adobe Printing Open House — Tue Aug 11, 3:00 PM
item.description:
Terraforming Indiana: Terran Robotics has started their 2nd 3D-printed, permitted adobe home in Bloomington, and they're inviting the community out to celebrate and see their earthen construction robotics in action.
Terran Robotics is a Bloomington-based startup building AI-guided robots that 3D-print homes from local adobe (clay, aggregate, and straw), aiming to make housing more affordable and sustainable.
Address available upon RSVP: https://partiful.com/e/lg2m6uzcsRu1h7DtOQ1i
Hosted by Danny and Ryan Zaricki.

item.title: Mindfulness at the Museum — Thu Aug 13, 2:00 PM — SIDNEY AND LOIS ESKENAZI MUSEUM OF ART
item.description:
Join us at the museum and mentally recenter by making art or journaling, and make some time to check in with yourself! Join us for a therapist-selected art activity meant to help you feel more balanced and in control. No prior skills needed, just bring your heart and mind. This group meets Thursday from 2–3 p.m., excluding holidays and museum closures. Meetings are held in the Atrium of the Sidney and Lois Eskenazi Museum of Art. Food and beverages are permitted in the atrium, so participants are welcome to bring lunch.
Source: Eskenazi Museum of Art

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Mon Aug 17 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Mon Aug 17 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.description:

item.title: Mindfulness at the Museum — Thu Aug 20, 2:00 PM — SIDNEY AND LOIS ESKENAZI MUSEUM OF ART
item.description:
Join us at the museum and mentally recenter by making art or journaling, and make some time to check in with yourself! Join us for a therapist-selected art activity meant to help you feel more balanced and in control. No prior skills needed, just bring your heart and mind. This group meets Thursday from 2–3 p.m., excluding holidays and museum closures. Meetings are held in the Atrium of the Sidney and Lois Eskenazi Museum of Art. Food and beverages are permitted in the atrium, so participants are welcome to bring lunch.
Source: Eskenazi Museum of Art

item.title: AMP: The Mill Renovation Celebration — Thu Aug 20, 4:00 PM — The Mill
item.description:
AMP is The Mill's monthly civic gathering, bringing together founders, investors, and the wider community to see what's being built in Bloomington. This first AMP event also celebrates the completion of The Mill's renovation, which added 30 more individual workspaces, three new private offices, upgraded collaboration spaces, and an improved event space with better technology, acoustics, and privacy. Membership is now around 400, with every private office full.Program:- Remarks from Bloomington Mayor Kerry Thomson and Indiana University's Shannon Heider, VP for Government and Community Relations- Fireside chat with Simon Beverton and Michelle Cole- Session with Solution Tree CEO Dr. Cameron Rains and Paragraph partner Brad WislerOpen networking bookends the evening, with food and drink provided.Free and open to the community. Please RSVP Now!
Source: BloomingtonOnline Events
